headline: Sequence-based deep models predict gene regulation and chromatin features from DNA
label: Deep Learning Regulatory Genomics
summary: Deep sequence models are now being tested for regulatory predictability, methylation context and chromatin looping, not just expression prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised sequence modelling of gene regulation, increasingly enriched with methylation, chromatin conformation and TF occupancy. Several preprints extend sequence-based models: TSSF applies a two-stage selective Transformer across 70 human cell types, MethylSeqNet conditions pretrained DNA embeddings on CpG methylation, and CREP fine-tunes Enformer to classify enhancers, promoters and insulators. The Dark Regulome preprint offers a residualization-and-permutation diagnostic that separates predictability-driven from regulation-driven in-silico mutagenesis variance, directly relevant to variant interpretation. CLASH apportions chromatin loop strength among genetic variation, methylation and CTCF occupancy, while MINTsC infers multi-way interactions from single-cell Hi-C. Published work includes ChromCall, TSProm and a plant TF-binding model linking regulatory variants to traits. What is new is the attempt to separate learnable predictability from regulatory effect and to integrate epigenetic context into sequence models.
